From: Ranjit Singh <ranjit@neuroleap.ai>

Subject: Pricing snapshot and model list for POC

Hi Ben,

Thanks for taking a look yesterday. We are lining up a small internal POC to validate latency and hallucination characteristics for NeuroLeap’s diagnostic-assist feature. Before we commit infra/time, could you send a concise baseline: per-1M token rates for input vs output (IO split) for your hosted API, and the current list of supported model families (and short notes on recommended ones for low-latency vs high-quality).

Specifically:
- Standard per-1M token input rate and output rate for a typical mid-sized model (e.g. ~3B-7B class).
- Same for a high-quality model (approx GPT-4 class equivalent).
- Any standard volume discount buckets (e.g. 10M/50M/250M) and % off list.
- Are there trial/credit options for a 30-day evaluation?
- Any caveats on token counting (do you use input+output or bill separately?)

We’re hoping to keep the POC to ~10M tokens/month to start, and if the quality/latency looks good we’ll ramp. We will likely need a simple one-page rate sheet we can pass to procurement.

Thanks — cc’ing Alex who will run the POC.

—Ranjit
VP Product, NeuroLeap

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Pricing snapshot and model list for POC

Hi Ranjit — thanks for the clear ask. Below is a concise baseline we can use for procurement and the POC. I attached our Q3 hosted ratecard and a short eval checklist you can use with the team.

Baseline hosted (per 1M tokens) — billed as input and output separately (we show both):
- Redwood-Base (3–7B class, optimized for latency)
  - Input: $0.90 / 1M tokens
  - Output: $1.20 / 1M tokens
- Redwood-High (40B+ / quality-oriented, GPT-4 class equivalent)
  - Input: $3.00 / 1M tokens
  - Output: $4.50 / 1M tokens

Standard volume discount framework (hosted API):
- 0–10M tokens/mo: list rates above (no volume discount)
- 10M–50M tokens/mo: 10% off list
- 50M–250M tokens/mo: 18% off list
- 250M+ tokens/mo: tiered negotiation (typical starting point 25%+, includes reserved capacity options)

Notes:
- Billing: we charge input and output separately (so a roundtrip with 1k input + 2k output = 3k tokens billed).
- Taxes and any cloud egress charges are excluded from the per-token rates.
- Trial: we can provide a 30-day POC package that includes $5k in credits for hosted usage + 2 dedicated onboarding hours with an engineer (subject to exec approval).
- SLA/throughput: hosted baseline is best-effort; for predictable latency and throughput we recommend Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity) — we can outline estimated monthlies if you expect steady traffic.

Attached: redwood-hosted-ratecard-Q3-2029.pdf (summary rate sheet) and neuroleap-eval-checklist.docx (short list of prompts & perf metrics).

Next steps I suggest: 1) confirm target model (we can recommend after a quick survey of expected prompt lengths), 2) accept the POC credit, and 3) schedule a 30-minute tech sync this week to wire up the eval. Marissa — can you drop an onboarding slot for Ranjit + Alex later this week? Vivek — any notes to add on burst/billing?

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Account Exec, Redwood Inference

Hi Ranjit — quick follow-up on commercial options as you plan the POC and potential production ramp:

- Short-term POC: The $5k credit Ben mentioned should cover ~6–8M tokens on Redwood-Base (depending on IO split). We’ll apply it to your account once you confirm POC start date.
- Committed discounts: If you opt for a 12-month committed volume of >50M tokens/month, we can lock in a 20% discount and discounted ingress for a flat add-on; commitments are invoiced monthly.
- Reserved capacity (Dedicated): For teams that need <100ms p95 and stable throughput, Dedicated pricing is a separate agreement — we can provide a 30-day trial of dedicated capacity in a shared pilot pool for qualifying customers.

I attached a one-pager in the ratecard that shows example math for 10M vs 50M token scenarios. Ben — I left a note in the drive link with the sample HubSpot quote.
